name: 10-segment LED bar graph with resistor network
description: Ten separate red LEDs (high-efficiency red, 627 nm, VF 1.9 V typ / 2.3 V max at 10 mA, 30 mA max per segment) in one DIP-20 bar: pins 1-10 are the anodes of segments 1-10 and pins 20-11 their cathodes. Each cathode goes through one resistor of an 11-pin bussed 330 Ω network whose common pin goes to GND, so each GPIO drives one segment directly (high = on, about 4 mA from 3.3 V, 9 mA from 5 V). No chip, no supply pin. Sold as: Kingbright DC10EWA 10-segment red LED bar graph (DIP-20, also sold by SparkFun/Adafruit as "LED bar graph - red") together with a Bourns 4611X-101-331LF 11-pin bussed 330 Ω SIP resistor network; the 11 nets are A1-A10 and GND.
eli5: A row of ten little red lights in one block, like the volume meter on a stereo: switch on more pins and the bar grows longer.

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Anode of segment 1 (DIP pin 1); its cathode (DIP pin 20) goes through a 330 Ω network resistor to GND. GPIO high = segment 1 on, about 4 mA at 3.3 V. Segment 1 is the end next to the anode mark (pin 1).

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Common pin (pin 1, marked with the dot) of the 11-pin bussed resistor network: all ten cathode resistors join here. Connect to the microcontroller's GND.

supplierQuery: 10 segment LED bar graph DIP-20 red DC10EWA
buildNotes: Bar graph pin 1 is at the anode mark (chamfered corner / printed '+'): pins 1-10 along that side are the anodes A1-A10, and the opposite side runs 11-20, so segment n's cathode is pin 21-n (segment 1: pins 1 and 20).

Put the bar graph across the breadboard's centre gap with the anodes on the GPIO side. Plug the 11-pin bussed resistor network into the cathode row so its pins 2-11 meet cathode pins 20-11, and run its pin 1 (the dot, the common bus) to GND.

Never wire a segment without its resistor: a 3.3 V GPIO straight into a 1.9 V LED far exceeds the 30 mA limit. With 330 Ω each segment draws about (3.3 - 1.9) / 330 = 4 mA, all ten about 42 mA, inside the ESP32's and the Pico's total GPIO budget.
Reverse voltage is only 5 V: if the bar stays dark, it is probably in backwards: rotate it 180°. 3.3 V the wrong way round does not harm it (5 V is the limit).
Create every pin with value=0 so the bar starts dark; light segments 1..n for a level meter or one segment for a dot display.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from bargraph import BarGraph

bar = BarGraph([{A1}, {A2}, {A3}, {A4}, {A5}, {A6}, {A7}, {A8}, {A9}, {A10}])
while True:
    for n in (3, 8):
        bar.level(n)
        print('LEVEL %d' % n)
        time.sleep(2)

test.title: The bar shows 3 then 8 segments in turn
